title: Had this dream a few weeks ago. I wrote it down so i couldn't forget it. I swear I feel different about how I manage stress after this
content: The hum of the city had become a constant weight on James’ shoulders, pressing down on him like an invisible burden. The ceaseless demands of work, the expectations of life, and the unrelenting noise of existence gnawed at him day after day. He longed for escape, for a moment of silence where his mind could simply be still. It was on one such evening, weary from another long day, that James decided to cut through the mall on his way home, hoping to avoid the suffocating congestion of the busy intersection outside. The mall was its usual self: bright, bustling, and lined with stores he had passed a hundred times before. He let his feet carry him forward, his thoughts distant and tired, until something caught his eye. A flash of light in the corner of his eye that grabbed his attention. He slowed down to glance at the source of the light, but there was nothing, just a blank wall next to him. As he was about to continue his walk home, dismissing what he saw, he felt an inexplicable urge to look a little closer. He ran his fingers along the wall where he saw the flash emerge, and to his surprise, something seemed out of place. A large wall panel was slightly crooked in it's fitting, allowing a small sliver of light to emerge from behind it... but why would there be light behind a wall? James hesitated, then grasped its edge and carefully shifted it aside. What he saw made his breath hitch—a corridor, one he had never seen before. The hallway stretched forward, unfamiliar yet inviting. It was carpeted in deep, swirling hues of brown and red, soft and luxurious under his feet. The lighting was low, warm, golden—a stark contrast to the bright sterility of the mall he had known. The walls were a darker shade, richer, more intimate. But most notably, it was silent. Not an eerie, unnatural silence, but a perfect hush, punctuated only by the distant hum of escalators and the faint electric whisper of overhead lights. The human noise, the voices, the footsteps, the ever-present clamor of the outside world—gone. He stepped forward, crossing the threshold, and a sense of profound peace washed over him. Rounding the corner, his breath caught once again. The corridor opened into an enormous atrium, an endless expanse of mall unlike anything he had ever seen. Levels upon levels of softly lit stores rose infinitely upward, fading into a hazy glow at an impossible height. Every shop was pristine, perfectly arranged, their shelves stocked with beautiful things. The food court was a dream—every restaurant brimming with steaming, delicious meals, the aroma mingling in a tantalizing, mouthwatering harmony. Plush velvet couches and enormous beanbags beckoned from every corner, conversation pits with crackling stone fireplaces waiting with open arms. It was a sanctuary, untouched, uninterrupted, impossibly serene. James wandered, enraptured. As he walked through the toy store, he passed rows upon rows of what seemed to be all of his favorite, most joy-inspiring toys he had possessed over the course of his life—things he had long forgotten until they were right there in front of him, like welcome ghosts from the past. There were action figures he had once cherished, intricate model trains with tiny lights twinkling in their miniature windows, plush animals that looked as soft and comforting as they had in childhood. And there they were, brand new, in boxes, in endless quantities. His heart filled with the most inexplicable peace and healing. He was elated, euphoric. He sat for what felt like hours, playing his favorite childhood video games, the controllers familiar in his hands, the pixelated worlds pulling him in like an old friend. He built model planes, snapping the pieces together with care, feeling the simple joy of creation. He rode bikes around the aisles, their rubber tires whispering against the polished floor, the exhilaration of movement filling him with childlike glee. He played and laughed until his face hurt from smiling. His eyes welled with tears. He felt at home. Not home in the conventional sense, not the home where his family lived and he paid the electric bill, but home on a deeper level. He felt at home within himself. He felt in touch with his true essence. He was transcending. He was happy. From there, he wandered further, discovering a bookstore filled with towering shelves of every book he had ever loved, as well as ones he had always meant to read. He sank into a plush armchair, the smell of paper and ink surrounding him, and lost himself in page after page. Hours passed—at least, they should have. A sudden worry stirred in his chest. He fumbled for his phone, checking the time, expecting to see the night slipping away. But the screen glowed back at him with an impossible truth. Not a minute had passed since he first stepped inside. Panic and wonder warred within him. He needed to leave. Needed to see if the world outside still existed as it should. He rushed through the long, quiet hallways, retracing his steps, feeling his pulse quicken. He reached the mirror, saw the glow of the mall beyond it, and stepped through. The noise returned in an instant. The same couple still walked ahead of him, as if not a moment had passed. The bustling mall was unchanged, indifferent to his absence. James stood there, reeling, then slowly, a smile curled at his lips. He felt lighter than he had in years. He told no one. That night, his wife greeted him with surprise and joy—he looked rested, at ease in a way she hadn’t seen in ages. He held her close, felt the warmth of home, and for the first time in a long time, felt truly present. The next day, he retraced his steps through the mall, heart pounding with anticipation. There it was—the panel, unmoved, waiting. He slipped behind it once more, and the sanctuary welcomed him back. Day after day, James returned. He wandered, explored, reveled in the peace of his secret haven. He spent what felt like weeks there, growing stronger, shedding the weight of stress and sorrow. And yet, in the real world, not a second was lost. He emerged each evening renewed, his burdens lighter, his heart full. Life outside flourished. His work improved, his laughter became genuine, his presence with his family and friends deeper and more meaningful. The secret space had given him a gift beyond time—it had given him himself. And so, James continued to return, day after day, to the endless, quiet halls of his hidden sanctuary, where peace was boundless, where time was kind, and where, at last, he was free
